notes: ⭐ 13/09/2026: THE COMMONS IS DEAD AND ITS CODE IS DELETED (Dean). The shipped game is the two-board Notice Board visit with no host draw: rules.turn.visitCurrency 'noticeBoardPower', rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed false and rules.economy.noticeBoardsBySeats {"2": 2, "3": 1, "4": 1}, with hostDrawOnVisit 0. The commonsTake, commonsThreshold, commonsColourMatch, commonsWildPair, commonsHarvestMin, commonsHarvestTake and unclaimedBoardsToCentre knobs went with it. Every overlay that sets visitCurrency 'card' or 'meeple', and each notice-board arm built on the old defaults, pins selfVisitAllowed and noticeBoardsBySeats.2 so it stays the game it was. Notes below that call the commons the shipped game are history.

⭐ storeCoinsPerCard AND coinSupplyPerPlayer ARE THE VILLAGE STORE (Dean, ruled 12/09/2026, ledger A150, V1 to V5 of docs/village-store-coins-2026-09-12-v2.md), AND BOTH SHIP AT 0, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OFF SWITCH: NOTHING IN THE GAME MINTS A COIN. 1 and 5 are the arm. THE MINT, and there is exactly one: when you make a delivery you may spend any number of additional cards FROM YOUR BARN and take one coin for each, and the exchange resolves AFTER the crate is paid (V3), so a player can never convert the cards the delivery itself needs. THE SUPPLY is SHARED and sized at coinSupplyPerPlayer times seats - 10 at two seats, 20 at four - with NO per-player holding cap: one player may hold all of them, and spent coins return to the supply and may be minted again (V4, V5). ⚠️ AN INT RATHER THAN A BOOL IN BOTH CASES, so the rate and the pool can be swept without another knob, which is this project's established preference. ⭐ WHY IT EXISTS, AND THE BETTER OF THE TWO ARGUMENTS IS DEAN'S OWN. The barn parity trap strands about 11 cards a player a game (88.8% of the time a player holds barn cards they cannot afford any open tile, and 84% of those are one or two cards short), and played decks reshuffle 7 / 6 / 4 times a game off a 12-card deck, so stranded cards are shrinking the CIRCULATING POOL rather than merely sitting there. A converted card goes to the discard and returns on the next reshuffle, which makes the exchange a lubrication rule as much as a sink, and reshuffles per played deck is therefore the cleanest falsifiable prediction in the pass: if the Store works, that number falls. ⛔ THE MINT MUST NOT BE BUILT AS A SUBSET ENUMERATION. "Spend any number of cards from your barn" is the POWER SET of the barn, and an 11-card barn offers 2,048 conversions in one task at every delivery, which is the discard enumerator's failure mode arriving through a new door - a 116,535-move position stopped this project on 02/09/2026 and an 888,030-move one on 05/09/2026. Build it as a repeated binary choice, "convert one more card, or stop", which turns 2^n into n sequential decisions and costs nothing in expressiveness because the player reaches every subset by a different route. ⛔ AND coinEconomy() IN packages/engine/src/setup.ts MUST BE EXTENDED to include storeCoinsPerCard above 0 or coinSupplyPerPlayer above 0, or the wallet will not exist when the Store is on. It is a serialisation question and never a rules question. ⚠️ THE ONE GUARD THAT IS A CARD RATHER THAN A KNOB: O17 The Fruit Basket is restricted to a card you discard FROM YOUR HAND (ruled 12/09/2026, the O17 ledger row), because as written a card paid into the exchange is a card you spend, so O17 would return it to the barn while its owner kept the coin. That is a SECOND MINT, and a second mint is what every coin economy in this project has died of. ⚠️ AND THE PLACEMENT IS ON TEST RATHER THAN SETTLED (C113): docs/village-store-2026-08-19-v1.md section 1 ruled out exactly this rider on Deliver as "no cost, so it is always correct". If the arm shows every player converting every spare card every time, the August verdict was right and the placement is what to change.

⭐ THE FOUR COIN-SINK LEAVES - coinPaysBuild, coinPaysSuitCost, coinPaysGrow and coinGrowOnFullBuilding - ARE V6 TO V9 (Dean, ruled 12/09/2026, ledger A150) AND ALL FOUR SHIP false. Read only where a coin can exist at all, which since 12/09/2026 means the Village Store above; nothing else mints one. A COIN IS A WILD CARD AND IT MAY BE SPENT ON EXACTLY TWO THINGS. BUILD (V6): any or all of a build cost INCLUDING the n-of-suit requirement, so three coins pays "2 apples and a wild", and Power and Endgame cards are included (V7), so two coins buys one. GROW (V8): activate a building, and THE COIN PLACES NOTHING, so the building does not advance toward its threshold and never clogs. ⭐ AND A FULL BUILDING IS A LEGAL TARGET (V9), the first clog bypass in this game since the meeples, ruled in deliberately: Dean's reason is that if you go through all the effort of getting cards in your barn, the reward should be awesome. ⛔ A COIN MAY NEVER PAY A VISIT, A HARVEST OR A DELIVERY (V10), coins score nothing at any rate (V11), and they do NOT count toward the tie-break of most cards in hand and barn combined (V12). ⛔ FOUR LEAVES RATHER THAN ONE, AND THAT IS THE 05/09/2026 LESSON APPLIED BEFORE THE FACT INSTEAD OF AFTER IT: ruling an arm in rules in its whole bundle, which has already shipped this project a passenger nobody argued for. coinPaysBuild and coinPaysGrow are two different bets - one converts barn into tableau, the other converts barn into repeatable abilities and deliberately suppresses harvesting - so if they go in together and the arm reads badly, nobody will know which did it. coinPaysSuitCost is split off coinPaysBuild because "coins pay wild costs only" and "coins pay everything" are meaningfully different games and it is one run to find out; it is also the first thing proposed that makes off-crop building and off-suit Powers cheap, against an own-crop build share that has sat near 83%. coinGrowOnFullBuilding is split off coinPaysGrow because it is the strongest single clause in the package. ⛔ AND IT IS MEANINGLESS ON ITS OWN: a full-building Grow that no coin can pay for is not a rule. Ask it through coinGrowReachesFullBuildings(data), which carries the precedence and is the one spelling every branch of play must use; the raw leaf is a knob description and a report header and nothing else. ⚠️ THE ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCES, ALL RULED WITH EYES OPEN: cards that trigger on a PLACEMENT do not fire on a coin-Grow (A16 The Beekeeper's Veil is the obvious one), A21 The Wax Hall does not count a building held empty by coin-Grows, and the Apiary board's bought Grow reaches a full building by the same clause, so expect the board mix to move off apiary 12%. ⛔ AND THE TIER 3 LAYER NEEDS RE-PRICING (C110): the cost/threshold curve is inverse ON PURPOSE, expensive low-threshold buildings are strong BECAUSE clog is their brake, and a repeatable currency that removes the brake changes what every Tier 3 is worth. Card-balance work, not a reason to reopen the rule, and not a reason to hold up the arm. ⚠️ THE BUILD SINK IS THE BRANCHING RISK, AND IT IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO EXPLODE: payments are already C(hand, k) and coins add every split of j coins and k minus j cards, so the count becomes a sum of binomials. COINS ARE FUNGIBLE, so the enumerator must treat the coin component as a COUNT and never as a choice of WHICH coins; getting that wrong is the single easiest way to blow the simulator up. Run the branching bench before and after, and quote seconds per game beside both move populations (C99).

⭐ deliveryMeepleSpace IS M1 OF THE DELIVERY MEEPLE (Dean, ruled 12/09/2026, ledger A151, section 5 of docs/village-store-coins-2026-09-12-v2.md), SHIPPED null. ⛔ AND null DOES NOT MEAN "NO MEEPLES", WHICH IS THE ONE THING A READER WILL ASSUME AND THE ONE THING THAT WOULD BREAK NINE FIXTURES: null means FALL THROUGH TO THE EXISTING meeplesPerTile() SEEDING, UNCHANGED. The commons and the notice-board visit still seed none, the v31 control still seeds one per delivery space, and the meeple loop still seeds island.meeples.seededSpaces. 1 is the rule Dean ruled in: exactly ONE meeple, on delivery space index 1 and never index 0, which is the 3 VP second delivery. ⛔ ASK IT THROUGH tileMeepleSpaces(data), which carries that precedence and is the one spelling every branch of play must use; the raw leaf is a knob description and a report header and nothing else. ⚠️ AN INDEX RATHER THAN A BOOLEAN, so space 0 can be swept if anybody ever asks. ⭐ THE CLAIM HALF IS ALREADY BUILT, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS ONE LEAF AND NOT A SUBSYSTEM: IslandTileState.meeples is parallel to deliveredBy BY INDEX, so the seat at deliveredBy[i] took meeples[i], and Dean's rule is the 04/09/2026 island seed meeple narrowed to space 1. ⭐ WHY IT EXISTS: THE ISLAND HAS NO DECISION IN IT. Every tile is mechanically identical, no levels and no ascending VP, so the only island choice is "take 6 before 3" and it is the same every time. A random reward on the second space makes taking second place a real choice, and one whose value changes over the game. ⭐ AND IT RESTORES THE ONLY CATCH-UP TERM THIS DESIGN EVER HAD, deleted with the island's seed meeple on 09/09/2026 and never replaced. ⛔ IT IS NOT THE MEEPLE THAT DIED AT A TABLE ON 09/09/2026, AND THERE IS A NUMBER FOR THAT: second deliveries are 37.5% of all receipts and players make about 4.7 deliveries a game, so this mints roughly 1.8 meeples per player per game, each earned by deliberately taking second at a tile, where the rejected version seeded FIVE PER PLAYER at setup and the complaint was precisely that the bonus was always available. ⭐ ITS PROVENANCE IS A TABLE RATHER THAN A RUN: Dean played it on 11/09/2026 and reported that it allowed some fun, powerful combos.

⭐ meepleSpendTiming, meepleSpendPerTurn AND meepleSpendDistinctColours ARE THE MEEPLE SPEND WINDOW (M4 and M5, Dean 12/09/2026, ledger A151 and C112), SHIPPED AT 'start', null and false, WHICH IS THE GAME EXACTLY AS IT IS PLAYED TODAY. The rule they reach: AFTER YOUR MAIN ACTION you may discard ONE meeple to take the PLAIN action of its colour, and the meeple then leaves the game. The colour mapping is wheat Harvest, vegetable Deliver, orchard Draw 2 keep both, apiary GROW and dairy Build - ⛔ GROW AND NOT SOW, because Sow is not a core action and orange meaning one thing in one place and another elsewhere has cost this project a day before - and ⛔ THE PLAIN ACTION AND NEVER THE NOTICE BOARD POWER, because the Orchard board is Draw 4 where the plain action is Draw 2 and the two stopped being the same thing on 10/09/2026 (M6, M7). ⛔ TWO OF THE THREE SHIPPED VALUES DIFFER FROM SECTION 3 OF docs/village-store-coins-handoff-2026-09-12-v1.md, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS DELIBERATE AND IS AN INERTNESS CORRECTION. The handoff ships meepleSpendTiming at 'none' and meepleSpendPerTurn at 0, and BOTH OF THOSE DELETE A PHASE THAT IS LIVE IN A NAMED CONTROL. overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json sets startingMeeplesPerColour 1 beside visitCurrency 'card', under which meepleOptions (packages/engine/src/actions.ts) returns a real list and the turn-start meeple spend runs, exactly as turnflow.ts's own header documents the v31 turn: "spend any number of MEEPLES, one at a time". packages/sim/fixtures/2p-v31-opening.json replays against it. So 'start' IS the current behaviour and is therefore the inert value, 'none' stays reachable as a third value, and 'afterAction' is M4's arm; and null means UNLIMITED, in the established idiom of commonsThreshold, commonsHarvestTake and meepleCapPerColour, where 0 would mean "no spend at all". A shipped value that silently changes a control is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson wearing a new costume, and a control that moves is not a control. ⚠️ meepleSpendDistinctColours IS C112 AND IT IS A SEPARATE LEAF ON PURPOSE. Dean ruled ONE PER TURN on a branching-explosion concern, but the concern shrank when it was measured - at about 1.8 meeples a player a game, "as many as you like" almost never means more than two - while the combo burst is the thing his own table enjoyed on 11/09/2026, so the cap of 1 removes exactly what the provenance liked. The alternative rule is "no two of the same colour", which is NOT expressible as an integer, so meepleSpendPerTurn alone cannot reach it: the arm as Dean ruled it is meepleSpendPerTurn 1 with this false, and the C112 variant is meepleSpendPerTurn null with this true. ⛔ A SECOND LEAF RATHER THAN A MAGIC VALUE OF meepleSpendPerTurn, for the reason hostDrawCapPerRound is a second leaf beside hostDrawOnVisit: this project has twice paid for a quantity that changed meaning underneath a published reading (a17 judged on plays per turn on 09/09/2026, and the meeple cap that shipped as a passenger on 05/09/2026). meepleSpendPerTurn keeps meaning HOW MANY; this says WHICH ONES MAY BE COMBINED. ⚠️ AND M4'S TIMING REVERSES THE REASON THE BONUS SITS AT THE FRONT: the bonus was moved to the start of the turn on Dean's own reasoning that a turn visibly ends on the main action (C2, 09/09/2026), and a meeple spend after it means the turn ends on a bonus again. Mild, because most turns will have no meeple to spend, but it is a direct tension with a deliberate ruling and it is recorded rather than discovered. ⚠️ TWO ENGINE RULINGS ARE OWED AND NEITHER IS A LEAF: whether the spend is legal on a turn whose main action was PASSED rather than taken (D7 of the handoff), and whether the standing rule that an action you cannot legally perform is not offered applies here, which would make a meeple UNDISCARDABLE (D8, "yes" indicated).

⭐ hostDrawOnVisit IS S17, THE HOST DRAW (Dean, ruled 11/09/2026), SHIPPED AT 0 AND READ ONLY UNDER rules.turn.visitCurrency 'noticeBoardPower'. 0 changes nothing; 1 is the rule Dean ruled in: WHEN A NEIGHBOUR VISITS YOU, YOU DRAW A CARD, immediately, off a deck. ⭐ ITS PROVENANCE IS A TABLE RATHER THAN A SIMULATION, which is rare enough here to be worth recording: Dean played overlays/notice-board-visit-two-boards-v1.overlay.json at a two-player table on 11/09/2026, house-ruled this in during the session, and reported that the visiting worked well, that everyone visited, that every Notice Board was used at some stage, and that "the rule that the person who gets visited draws a card led to a lot of extra cards in play, which relieved the tightness of the game in a useful way". ⛔ IT AMENDS S7 OF docs/notice-board-visit-handoff-2026-09-10-v2.md, WHICH SAID THE OPPOSITE IN AS MANY WORDS: S7 reads that the card stays on the board it was played to and its owner harvests it into their barn, "and that is the payment and there is no other". Under S17 there is now one other and it is paid INSTANTLY, so the host is paid twice - once in a card drawn now, once in material harvested later. Do not quote S7 forward without this amendment. ⭐ IT IS THE SANCTIONED SHAPE AND NOT A BANNED ONE: RESTOCK was banned as a per-interaction BANK faucet, and the standing rule beside that ban reads "if a give-cards effect returns, it pays in draws". A host draw comes off a deck. It also fits the lens the last seven versions of this bonus slot failed: PAY THE GIVER IN THE SAME ACT, OR THE GIVER DRAWS THE CHARGE - S7 pays the host in deferred material they must harvest and then deliver, S17 pays them in the same act. ⚠️ AND THE COST IS REAL: EVERY VISIT NOW ADDS A CARD TO THE GAME, at about 14.4 visits received per player per game at two seats under the control arm. ⛔ A SELF-VISIT MUST NEVER PAY IT - rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed is false on the arm that matters, and a card drawn for visiting yourself is a pure faucet paid by nobody. ⛔ AND THE SIMULATOR CANNOT MEASURE THE EFFECT DEAN LIKED: the engine's hand limit of 7 is an INSTRUMENT BOUND (C7) and the table plays with none, so the instrument clips exactly the extra cards in hand that relieved the tightness. A run answers the bonus rate, the barn glut, game length, deliveries and the hook; it cannot answer whether the game feels less tight, and no report of this arm may be quoted as evidence that it does. overlays/notice-board-visit-host-draw-v1.overlay.json is the arm and overlays/notice-board-visit-two-boards-v1.overlay.json is its control.

⭐ hostDrawCapPerRound IS THE HOST-DRAW CAP, SHIPPED false AND READ ONLY WHEN rules.turn.hostDrawOnVisit IS ABOVE 0. true means A HOST IS PAID AT MOST ONCE BETWEEN THEIR OWN TURNS, however many neighbours visit them in the meantime. ⛔ IT IS A SECOND LEAF RATHER THAN A CHANGE OF hostDrawOnVisit'S MEANING, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE: re-pointing the existing knob at a per-round quantity would silently redefine every number already published against it (the 17:23 report, a21-host-draw, the host-draw overlay's own description), and this project has twice paid for a quantity that changed underneath a published reading - a17 judged on plays per turn on 09/09/2026, and the meeple cap that shipped as a passenger on 05/09/2026. hostDrawOnVisit keeps meaning CARDS PER PAYMENT; this says HOW OFTEN A PAYMENT MAY HAPPEN. ⚠️ "PER ROUND" MEANS PER THE HOST'S OWN TURN CYCLE AND NOT PER THE VISITOR'S TURN, AND THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT. A cap on the VISITOR'S turn would bite only when one visitor sends two visits to the same host in a single turn, which is reachable at two seats alone (A Helping Hand against a rival holding two boards), and would leave FOUR SEATS - the only seat count that breaches - untouched. The latch is cleared when the HOST'S own turn begins. ⛔ WHY IT EXISTS: THE FOUR-SEAT BREACH. With hostDrawOnVisit 1 the bonus slot reads 64.9% of turns at four seats against Dean's 60% ceiling, where its one-leaf control reads 59.9% (reports/watchlist-2026-09-11T17-23-27-reference-v15-notice-board-visit-host-draw-v1.txt against reports/watchlist-2026-09-11T17-20-12-reference-v15-notice-board-visit-two-boards-v1.txt). The faucet scales with the number of rivals and a cap per host per round is the shape that stops it scaling. ⚠️ AND IT IS EXPECTED TO BE INSUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN, WRITTEN DOWN BEFORE THE RUN SO THE PREDICTION CAN BE SCORED: measured host draws per host per round are 0.489 / 0.553 / 0.787 by seat count, so a cap of one removes only the rounds that carried two or more - at most 21% / 24% / 31% of the faucet on a Poisson upper bound, and less in truth because bots spread visits across targets rather than piling on. The faucet buys 5.0 points at four seats, so a 31% cut returns about 1.5 and lands near 63.4%, still over the ceiling. If the run reads much better than that, the arrival distribution is more clustered than Poisson and THAT is the finding. overlays/notice-board-visit-host-draw-capped-v1.overlay.json is the arm and overlays/notice-board-visit-host-draw-v1.overlay.json is its one-leaf control.

⚠️ 13/09/2026: SHIPPED AT {"2": 2, "3": 1, "4": 1} SINCE THE COMMONS WAS DELETED; the overlays that relied on one board each at two seats pin "2": 1. The note below predates the flip. ⭐ noticeBoardsBySeats IS DEAN'S TWO-BOARD FIX (Dean, ruled 11/09/2026), SHIPPED AT ONE BOARD EACH AT EVERY SEAT COUNT SO IT CHANGES NOTHING, AND READ ONLY UNDER rules.turn.visitCurrency 'noticeBoardPower' WITH rules.turn.selfVisitAllowed false. It is a map keyed by seat count, in the idiom of island.decksInPlayBySeats and island.demandTokensBySeats, and it says how many Notice Boards each player lays out. At 2 it means each player lays out TWO: their own suit's board, plus one more drawn AT RANDOM from the suits nobody is farming. The fifth board is not used. At 3 and 4 it is one each and the rest are unused, which is exactly overlays/notice-board-visit-no-self-v1.overlay.json, so the arm differs from that control AT TWO SEATS ONLY. ⭐ WHY IT EXISTS, AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Four corners of a 2x2 were run at 4,820 games each on 11/09/2026. With self-visits ON and no centre the bonus rate read 71.2% and the hook 0.44, a FAIL; with self-visits ON and the centre on, 78.4% and 0.23, a FAIL; with self-visits OFF and the centre on, 64.7% and 0.31, a FAIL; and with self-visits OFF and no centre, 46.1% and 0.54, THE ONLY CORNER IN WHICH THE HOOK PASSES AND THEREFORE THE ONLY VERSION IN WHICH THE DESIGN'S OWN THESIS WORKS. That corner STARVES AT TWO PLAYERS: the bonus is used on 28.8% of turns against Dean's 30% floor, and 17.9% of two-player turns begin with cards in hand and no legal visit, because with self-visiting banned and one board each there is exactly ONE board a seat may visit. The unclaimed-boards centre fixed the rate and DESTROYED the cross-table traffic - at two players only 14.7% of plays reached a person - and the structural lesson it measured is the reason for this knob: THERE ARE ONLY EVER FOUR TARGETS, AND EVERY TARGET ADDED THAT IS NOT A PERSON DILUTES THE PERSON. ⭐ THIS ADDS TARGETS THAT ARE PEOPLE. Targets become 2 / 2 / 3 by seat count (at 2 seats one rival holding two boards, at 3 seats two rivals holding one each, at 4 seats three rivals holding one each) and EVERY ONE OF THEM IS A PERSON, so the hook is not diluted. A seat still may never visit its own board, either of them. ⭐ AND THE RANDOM BOARD PAYS ITS OWNER: its power is usable only by rivals, but every fee paid onto it rests there until its OWNER harvests it into their barn, so a popular board is income. That is this design's core loop, arriving on a board whose power its owner can never use. ⚠️ THE MAP HAS AN ARITHMETIC CEILING NOBODY HAS PRICED: the suits nobody is farming number (5 - seats), so an extra board each is only feasible where seats x (n - 1) is at most (5 - seats). That is 2 boards at two seats (2 drawn from 3, one left over) and ONE board at three and four seats. A sweep of {"3": 2} asks for six boards out of five and is not realisable without changing the card count; what an engine does with an infeasible value is an ENGINE ruling and it has not been made. ⚠️ AND A REAL CONSEQUENCE NOBODY HAS PRICED: at two seats a player owns TWO boards, so they have two income streams to harvest and twice the harvesting to do, and A21 The Wax Hall (1 VP for each of your buildings holding a card) can count TWO Notice Boards rather than one. rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold applies to each board separately, so the fee traffic a seat receives is split across two boards and each fills at half the rate, which is the a20 stall reading pointed at a new subject. overlays/notice-board-visit-two-boards-v1.overlay.json is the arm and overlays/notice-board-visit-no-self-v1.overlay.json is its control.

⚠️ 13/09/2026: SUPERSEDED - THE NOTICE BOARD VISIT IS NOW THE GAME and the commons is deleted. The note below predates the flip. ⭐ THE NOTICE BOARD VISIT IS AN ARM AND NOT THE GAME (Dean, 10/09/2026, docs/notice-board-visit-handoff-2026-09-10-v2.md, rules S1-S16). THE SHIPPED GAME IS STILL THE COMMONS. What the arm is, in one line: the centre is deleted, the five Notice Board cards go home to their owners' farms and are BUILDINGS again, and the bonus is to play one card from your hand onto ANY player's Notice Board - your own included - and immediately take that board's PRINTED POWER, with the card resting on the host's board until the host harvests it into their barn, which is the host's whole payment. It is reached by rules.turn.visitCurrency 'noticeBoardPower', a FOURTH value rather than a repointing of 'card': 'card' is the v31 control and carries three passengers this design does not want (a BLOCKING Notice Board threshold of 2, the standalone free Draw 1 in the bonus slot, and the turn-start meeple spend), and repointing it would silently change one of the three named controls the arm is read against. overlays/notice-board-visit-v1.overlay.json is the arm and pins every passenger by name; -no-self-v1, -blocking-v1, -threshold-2-v1 and -threshold-4-v1 are its four sub-arms. ⛔ TWO BASE VALUES MOVED WITH IT AND BOTH ARE PASSENGERS SOMEBODY ELSE HAS TO PIN. (1) rules.economy.noticeBoardThreshold is 3 where it was 2, which is S8's `3+`, so overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json now pins 2 by name and the printed card face still says 2. (2) rules.economy.farmsteadPower is RENAMED to rules.economy.noticeBoardPower and repointed to the S12 powers as amended by Dean's rulings C88 and C89 of 10/09/2026 - a knob whose name no longer describes it is worse than a new one - so the coins arm's Farmstead handler reads a block that has moved. Name the passengers before ruling, not after.

⭐ noticeBoardBlocks IS THE `3+` RULE, SHIPPED false (Dean, 10/09/2026, S8), AND IT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS CODEBASE HAS SPLIT "harvestable" FROM "accepts a card". false: three is the MINIMUM before the owner may harvest a Notice Board and never a maximum load - cards can always be added, nothing ever blocks, and the owner alone chooses when to cash in. true is the PAIRED CONTROL and makes the board an ordinary clogging building, so "does a board stall?" is measured rather than argued: that stall is a documented failure in the predecessor, the game stops when nobody wants to load, a blocking board can be shut by an owner who declines to harvest, and at two players there are only two boards. ⚠️ The face must print `3+` and not `3`, because the plus sign is the only thing telling a reader it is a floor rather than a ceiling. overlays/notice-board-visit-blocking-v1.overlay.json is the control.

THE TWO GAMES THE COMMONS REPLACED ARE CONTROLS AND THEIR CODE IS NOT DEAD. overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json is the v31 card visit of 02-04/09/2026; overlays/meeple-loop-v1.overlay.json is the v1 meeple loop of 04/09/2026; overlays/meeple-economy-v1.overlay.json is the meeple ECONOMY of 05/09/2026, which is the reference-v14 game and the last rules a report quotes. THE STANDING RULE THAT KEEPS THEM: a branch whose only producer is a knob at its shipped value is NOT deleted. ⚠️ AND THE 05/09/2026 LESSON THAT COST THIS PROJECT A RULING: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to PIN every knob the flip moved, so each of those three now pins visitCurrency, bonusTiming, startingMeeplesPerColour and the Orchard door's draw beside whatever it was already pinning. Name the passengers before ruling an arm in, not after.

THE ORCHARD DOOR IS DRAW 2 AND THAT IS A CHOICE, NOT AN INHERITANCE (Dean, 09/09/2026). workers.roster.draw.draw is 2/2 in the shipped data, where it was 3/3 for the whole life of the card visit. The self-cancellation law that made it 3 - a door priced in its own output currency has to over-deliver against the free Draw 1 - died with the free Draw 1 on 04/09/2026 and has no subject here either. ⚠️ BUT THE COMMONS PUTS A FEE BACK ON THE BONUS: a play costs a card, so a Draw 2 door returns 2 for 1 and nets +1, which is thinner than any other door's return. Whether that leaves the Orchard board dead is the one contested door number in the game and overlays/commons-draw-three.overlay.json is the arm. The v31 control pins 3/3 because that game measured with it.

The numbers that belong to no single card: setup quantities, the turn's shape, the one standing economy rate and the end-game trigger. Anything PRINTED on a card lives in cards.json instead, anything printed on the island lives in island.json, and the five door actions live in workers.json.

SCHEMA VERSION 2 IS v31 (Dean, 02/09/2026, docs/design-changes-v31-2026-09-02-v1.md). The bump is not cosmetic: the file lost seven keys in one edit and every one of them was a coin. If you are reading a v31 number against a report written before 02/09/2026, stop - the reference was re-cut as reference-v10 and no historical number in reports/ is comparable.

THERE ARE NO COINS. Not zero coins: no coin. Nothing is earned in them, nothing is priced in them, there is no coin tie-break and there is no coin knob. What went with the currency, in one list so nobody re-derives it from an old doc: startingCoins, upgradeCostCoins (there are no starter upgrades at all now), coinPityDivisor, visitPayout in all four of its branches, giftDiscardCoins, buyCost (the card buy) and marketCost (buy at market). Six of those seven were already null or already deleted in spirit by 19/08/2026; the seventh, the upgrade price, went with the upgraded faces. The design reason is the standing finding the market note used to carry, taken all the way: money is what buys SOLITAIRE in this game, because a visit is bought with a card and every other bonus option was bought with a coin, so a coin sink in the bonus slot crowds the visit out all game. The commons buys an action for a card with no supply to run out, so it could go either way. rules.endGame.deliveriesToTrigger is the knob and overlays/end-trigger.sweep.json is the ladder.

THE BARN GLUT IS UNTOUCHED at +0.5 to +1.0 across four arms, and the commons hands it a new faucet (a harvested central pile) and a new drain (a card a turn leaving the hand for the centre). It is the oldest unfixed reading in the project and the wild substitution is still the only thing that has ever moved it.

THE VEGETABLE DOOR COLLAPSED under both previous versions - 18% of door uses under v31, 8% under the meeple economy - and Deliver is the scoring action. The candidate mechanism nobody has tested: Deliver is the one door whose value depends entirely on the BUYER's barn, so making it cheap does not make it usable. Watch whether the central Harvest, which fills a barn without a building, finally gives the Vegetable board something to be worth.

WHETHER INTERACTION IS A PER-TURN OR A PER-GAME QUANTITY, which is the old hook question surviving its own subject. a08-the-hook has NO SUBJECT under the commons - there is no neighbour to visit - and a18-commons-traffic replaces it, so the same choice has to be made again about plays per turn against plays per game before either number can pass or fail anything.

THE MONOCULTURE PULL (v31 risk 3). The Farmstead pays 1 VP per own-suit card built and the Power and Endgame cards cost 2 cards of their own suit; the own-crop build share was 82.6% before and 83.3% after, and it has not been read under either meeple pass or this one. The commons pushes the other way for the first time - any card pays for any board - so this is worth re-reading rather than assuming.

THE INTERFACE IS NOW TWO VERSIONS BEHIND. packages/ui pins itself to overlays/v31-card-visit.overlay.json and draws the v31 game: a Notice Board per player, a fill bar, a visit assembled by dragging a card. It never grew the meeple loop and it does not have the commons either. ⭐ THE ENCOURAGING HALF: the commons is a SIMPLER interface than either meeple version - five piles in the centre, drag a card onto one - so the debt is bigger and the job is smaller. See the docblock on `data` in packages/ui/src/session/table.ts.

THE 2-SEAT GAME IS STILL THE SEAT COUNT WITH THE LEAST EVIDENCE BEHIND IT. deliveriesToTrigger is flat, the island is half-used at 12 spaces, and the commons removes the one thing 2p was worst at (one rival board to visit) by putting all five boards in the middle. That is the change most likely to read differently at two seats than at four.
